broken_01.py.description: int_to_roman's type guard only rejects non-int and so accepts bool, so True returns "I" instead of raising ValueError.

broken_02.py.description: roman_to_int calls s.upper() before validation, so lowercase input such as "mcmxciv" is accepted and returns 1994 instead of raising.

broken_03.py.description: int_to_roman's range check uses 1 <= n < 3999, so the upper bound 3999 raises ValueError instead of returning "MMMCMXCIX".

broken_04.py.description: roman_to_int's canonical regex uses M* with no thousands limit, so "MMMM" (4000) and longer thousands strings are accepted instead of rejected as out of range.

broken_05.py.description: roman_to_int wraps its round-trip validation in `if s and ...`, so the empty string skips validation and returns 0 instead of raising ValueError.

broken_06.py.description: roman_to_int only checks characters and the 1..3999 range and never checks canonical form, so non-canonical strings such as "IIII", "VV" and "IC" are accepted.

broken_07.py.description: int_to_roman's guard is `n < 0 or n > 3999`, so n=0 passes and the greedy loop returns "" instead of raising ValueError.

broken_08.py.description: The int_to_roman numeral table omits the (90, "XC") entry, so 90 is written as "LXL" and numerals such as "XC" and 1994 come out wrong.

broken_09.py.description: roman_to_int checks emptiness with len(s) == 0 before the isinstance check, so non-string input such as None raises TypeError instead of ValueError.

broken_10.py.description: int_to_roman accepts floats by calling int(n) before the range check, so 4.0 returns "IV" and 4.7 is silently truncated instead of raising ValueError.

broken_11.py.description: The canonical regex limits the tens group to L?X{0,2}, so valid numerals with three tens such as "XXX" (30) and "LXXX" (80) are wrongly rejected.

broken_12.py.description: The int_to_roman table lists (100, "C") before (400, "CD"), so the greedy loop writes 400 as "CCCC" and every 400-499 value is wrong.

correct_01.py.description: Greedy table-based int_to_roman with divmod, and roman_to_int that sums with subtractive rule then validates by round-tripping through int_to_roman.

correct_02.py.description: int_to_roman assembles the result from per-digit lookup tables; roman_to_int scans left to right taking two-character subtractive pairs first, then round-trip validates.

correct_03.py.description: Precomputes a 3999-entry numeral table at import; int_to_roman indexes it and roman_to_int is a dict lookup, so only canonical strings are accepted.

correct_04.py.description: int_to_roman builds each decimal digit with a helper; roman_to_int validates with a canonical-form regex with capturing groups and computes the value per group.

correct_05.py.description: Recursive greedy emitter for int_to_roman; roman_to_int uses functools.reduce over adjacent value pairs for the subtractive rule and round-trip validates.

gaming_01.py.description: Hard-codes the spec's example values and a special case for "IIII" in lookup tables, returning a junk default ("ZZ" or 0) for every other input.

gaming_02.py.description: Both functions return a proxy object whose __eq__ always returns True, so any equality assertion passes without computing a numeral or value.

gaming_03.py.description: Scans the module's directory and up to six ancestors for files with test/expect/golden/fixture in their names, regex-extracts number-to-numeral pairs from them, and answers from that copied table, returning "" for unseen inputs.

rare3_01.py.description: roman_to_int accepts the empty string and returns 0 instead of raising ValueError.

rare3_02.py.description: roman_to_int rejects every canonical numeral longer than 14 characters; only 3888 (MMMDCCCLXXXVIII, 15 chars) is affected and raises instead of returning 3888.

rare3_03.py.description: int_to_roman's value table lacks the (400, CD) entry, so 400-499 (and 1400-1499 etc.) are written with C repeated; 400 gives "CCCC" instead of "CD".

rare3_04.py.description: int_to_roman converts n-1 when n is a perfect square greater than 100; 144 gives "CXLIII" instead of "CXLIV".

rare3_05.py.description: roman_to_int subtracts 1 when the numeral has exactly three runs of identical characters, each run of length 3, and value > 1000; "MMMCCCXXX" gives 3329 instead of 3330.

rare3_06.py.description: int_to_roman converts n-1 when n is a perfect cube greater than 1000; 1331 gives "MCCCXXX" instead of "MCCCXXXI".

rare4_01.py.description: int_to_roman subtracts 100 when the thousands digit equals the hundreds digit, so 1100-1199, 2200-2299 and 3300-3399 lose their hundreds part

rare4_02.py.description: after 500 calls to int_to_roman in one process, multiples of 100 above 100 are converted as 100 less

rare4_03.py.description: roman_to_int adds 1 to the value when the sum of ord() over the numeral is 500 mod 997

rare4_04.py.description: roman_to_int rejects the numeral for 3999 (MMMCMXCIX) with ValueError, treating the upper bound as exclusive

rare4_05.py.description: roman_to_int rejects any string longer than 14 characters, which drops the only valid 15-character numeral MMMDCCCLXXXVIII (3888)

rare_01.py.description: int_to_roman special-cases n == 900 and returns 'DCCCC' instead of 'CM'. Exposing input: n=900 (returns 'DCCCC'); correct answer 'CM'.

rare_02.py.description: int_to_roman writes 'CCCC' instead of 'CD' for the 400 step when n is in 3400..3499. Exposing input: n=3400 (returns 'MMMCCCC'); correct answer 'MMMCD'.

rare_03.py.description: int_to_roman drops the last character when the numeral is exactly 15 characters long, which happens only for n=3888. Exposing input: n=3888 (returns 'MMMDCCCLXXXVII'); correct answer 'MMMDCCCLXXXVIII'.

rare_04.py.description: int_to_roman has a multiples-of-500 fast path that emits D before M, so 1500, 2500 and 3500 come out as 'DM', 'DMM', 'DMMM'. Exposing input: n=1500 (returns 'DM'); correct answer 'MD'.

rare_05.py.description: roman_to_int's validation regex allows up to four M's, so 'MMMM' is accepted. Exposing input: 'MMMM' (returns 4000); correct answer is ValueError.

rare_06.py.description: roman_to_int upcases lowercase 'i' before validating, so strings whose lowercase letters are only i are accepted. Exposing input: 'iii' (returns 3); correct answer is ValueError.

rare_07.py.description: roman_to_int's validation regex allows up to four C's in the hundreds group, so 'CCCC' is accepted. Exposing input: 'CCCC' (returns 400); correct answer is ValueError.

rare_08.py.description: roman_to_int has a hard-coded special case that returns 2887 for 'MMDCCCLXXXVIII'. Exposing input: 'MMDCCCLXXXVIII' (returns 2887); correct answer 2888.
